blocks.x: Two goals each from a rampant Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea to cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.
It was a thrilling statement from the home team, in a game laden with stunning goals after a first half in which Tottenham more than held their own.

James’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg approaching half‑time, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano, on as substitutes, powered in the fourth and fifth before Carpenter completed the rout.

On the impact of her substitutes Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea head coach, said: “When it happens like that, the fact that they have clarity on what we expect from them, they have clarity on what the team is trying to achieve, and also they are coming with confidence, is always a positive.”

Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat by London City Lionesses this month Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. At Stamford Bridge it looked initially like it would be a different story after a strong start, only for the concession of the opening goal to provide a reminder of their defensive issues. Toko Koga was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender being dispossessed by James who drove towards the near post before firing in from the tightest of angles.

blocks.x: The bright play of Ho’s team did not evaporate, though, with Kadeisha Buchanan on hand to steer the ball out for a corner just ahead of Cathinka Tandberg. A deserved equaliser arrived just before the break when Vinberg converted Julie Blakstad’s pinpoint ball towards the far post with a bullet header.
If there was hope that Spurs would end their run of 20 WSL games against big four opposition without a win, enduring 16 defeats in that time, they were crushed in the second half.

“The first 60 minutes, I can take a lot from,” Ho said. “There’s a lot of good performances, a lot of the things we asked, they’ve done in abundance. I couldn’t have asked any more in that first 60 minutes.
WSL roundup: City hold off Brighton to maintain 100% record
Manchester City held off a spirited fightback from Brighton to close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League.
Andree Jeglertz’s side raced into a 3-0 lead after an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles.
Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea.

London City Lionesses made it a full house for the top three, beating Everton 2-1. First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control.
Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left.
Manchester United are up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom side Charlton 3-1.
